chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan al-Attar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man who slanders a group of people?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'With one statement?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said, 'He is given one Hadd (penalty). But if he differentiates between them in the slander, a Hadd is given to each one of them.'

key_terms.قَذَفَ: To slander or accuse of zina (unlawful sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for slandering a group collectively versus individually in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between general and specific slander (Qadhf) in Shia fiqh, establishing that a single general accusation incurs only one Hadd punishment, whereas specifying individuals multiplies the liability. This ruling underscores the principle of proportionality in penal law, ensuring that the severity of the punishment aligns with the precision of the accuser's claim. It reflects the Imams' emphasis on legal clarity to prevent excessive penalties for ambiguous statements.
